From Bharati to the Grammys: Inside Devan’s ‘Varuvaaiy’, the first Tamil song to earn a Grammy nomination
 How Chennai musicians Devan Ekambaram, Susha and Anil Srinivasan took a Subramania Bharati composition to the Grammys 
 Updated - November 17, 2026 05:50 pm IST 
 Srinivasa Ramanujam READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Musicians Devan Ekambaram, Susha and Anil Srinivasan. File
 | Photo Credit: Special arrangement
 “ Angikaaram (validation),” says singer-composer Devan Ekambaram excitedly over the phone, “This is recognition for my work in music for almost three decades.”
 He is referring to the recent honour for his latest independent song, ‘Varuvaaiy’ . A rare Subramania Bharati composition interpreted by Devan in a contemporary manner, ‘Varuvaaiy’ has earned a Grammy nomination in the Best Global Music Performance category. It is reportedly the first Tamil song to earn this recognition.
 Behind this track are three well-known Chennai musicians: Devan, singer Susha and pianist Anil Srinivasan.
 The global ear 
 ‘Varuvaaiy’ was born in June this year, when Devan was working on a full-fledged album of songs made by iconic Tamil poet and freedom fighter Subramania Bharati . A meeting with singer Susha sparked off the idea of ‘Varuvaai’. “My mother (Lakshmi Rangarajan) has a core memory with this particular song (’Varuvaai’) that was an ode to lord Krishna,” recalls Susha, who has been learning Carnatic music since she was five, “She had heard it at a concert and liked it so much that she had taken the effort to learn it. She recalled all that while teaching me this particular track, and I remembered that when Devan asked me to contribute to the album he was working on.”
 Susha’s vocals and Devan’s modern arrangements add flavour to ‘Varuvaai’, a number tuned in raga Desh, known to stir patriotic fervour. The duo’s distinctive collaboration — which combines the richness of Carnatic melodic traditions along with contemporary sounds — seems to have appealed to the global ear. Prakash Sontakke’s prowess with the Carnatic slide guitar in this track is a big value addition, as is Anil Srinivasan’s work on the piano. The popular pianist is elated at the nomination. “I am happy that it is Bharati on centrestage here — the grandest global one at that — and kudos to Devan and Susha for making it happen,” he says.
 Pianist Anil Srinivasan with singer Devan
 The next step 
 The Grammy nomination is a big deal for the team, which is currently mulling on a music video. “It is a big win for Bharati and Tamil indie music,” feels Devan, who has also contributed in the past to acclaimed albums such as Winds of Samsara (Ricky Kej and Wouter Kellerman), Divine Tides (Ricky Kej and Stewart Copeland) and Charu Suri’s Shayaan. 
 Devan has tried his luck at the Grammys before; in 2021, his ‘A Walk Through Brindavan’ track in Brindavan battled with 120 nominations from across the world but did not make it. Cut to 2026, and his ‘Varuvaai’ has made it to the top five from more than 500 global entries, rubbing shoulders with the likes of ‘Una Flor en Cada’ (KerreKe, Mireya Ramos and Alex E Chávez) ‘Orchestral’ (Angelique Kidjo, featuring Pharrel Williams and Quavo), ‘Porcelana’ (Rosalia and Dougie F) and ‘Dai Dai’ (Shakira and Burna Boy).
 Despite the star-studded names in the nominee list, some of whom have already bagged multiple Grammys on earlier occasions, Devan has his hopes pinned on ‘Varuvaaiy’. “We hope that the weeks to come will bring more attention to our song.”
 What is Sikkil Gurucharan’s ‘Jannal Oram’? From Ilaiyaraaja and Kamal Haasan to ‘Interstellar’ Devan is well-known to Tamil film music listeners of the 1990s, having worked extensively with composers like AR Rahman, Harris Jayaraj and Ilaiyaraaja . “I was a composer but singing opportunities came by, and I took them on,” recalls Devan, whose hit songs include ‘Oh Maria’ ( Kadhalar Dhinam ), ‘Macarina’ ( Kushi ) and ‘Ore Nyabagam’ ( Minnale ).
 Even as he rides the ‘Varuvaaai’ wave, Devan is also eyeing film composing assignments. Last featured as a composer in 2010 Tamil film Bale Pandiya , he is making a comeback with Pattarai , an upcoming Tamil-Telugu bilingual directed by Peter Allvin and starring JD Chakravarthy. “I’m looking forward to composing for films – because I entered the music industry with that aim,” he says, adding, “For now, all my focus is on taking ‘Varuvaaiy’ to the next level.”
 ‘Varuvaaai’ is available on all leading music streaming platforms
